reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction by Sundar Pichai from 2021. That doesn't prove there isn't one, because two of the main 2021 sources only partly opened.

- **BBC, Amol Rajan interview (aired July 2021):** The Internet Archive transcript showed only the first ten minutes or so. In that part, Pichai calls AI "the most profound technology that humanity will ever develop" but gives no date. The one timed line is about quantum computing, not AI: stable quantum computers are "probably still a decade away." So it's left out. I never saw the rest of the interview.
- **Stratechery interview (2021):** It wouldn't open ("url not allowed"), twice. Both failed attempts counted against my six page openings, so I couldn't quote it or check it.
- **Google I/O 2021 (his blog post, May 18):** He introduces LaMDA and the multimodal model MUM. The only time-bound promises are about TPU chips coming to cloud customers "later this year," which is a hardware plan, and quantum. Neither counts.
- **Bloomberg New Economy Forum (Nov 2021):** I only saw a Fortune news report on it. His forecasts there are about Search and business growth, with no AI date.
- **Stanford talk:** It does have a timed AI line (AI in healthcare "will still take a decade for it to fully play out"), but the page is dated June 2022. I listed it under other years.

I used all 6 page openings and 9 of the 12 searches. I didn't spend the last three, since I couldn't have opened anything they turned up. Next time, these are worth trying: a full BBC transcript or the podcast version, a working copy of the Stratechery interview, and his 2021 earnings-call transcripts.
